lines: One helmet, five mugs, and the spawn goes back in the plot. {drinks} drinks in our cellars and not one of them is water.
Brewed from the finest cave wheat. Tired of drinking the same old booze? So were we. Ask for a beer.
For artifacts, weddings and the end of a long mood. Also Tuesdays.
Pig tails grow in summer and autumn. Our ale grows on you.
The farmer's workshops have outdone themselves. Bring a loom. Bring two. Bring a cart.
Holding {seeds} seeds? You'll need bags. Brewing returns the seed; cooking doesn't. Plan accordingly.
Fortress cats hunt vermin and need no food. They will choose you. Resistance is not advised.
Trained at the kennels, fed by nobody: fortress dogs need no dinner. Ask for a loyal one.
The hospital wants all of it. Your shins will want it later.
The unburied may return within months as ghosts. Our coffins are roomy, our slabs well engraved. Book early.
Now performing at the tavern most evenings. Hecklers will be dealt with by the keeper.
Scholars write, scribes copy, we bind. Paper pressed from genuine pig tail slurry.
At war with {enemy}? Who isn't. Buy a policy today; collect it from your coffin.
A cut gem set into good work doubles its value. A rough gem in a bin doubles nothing. Bring them in.
The mountain listens the deeper you go. Our helmets don't help with that, but they do help with rocks.
Cowardly, scaly and everywhere. Call before they climb.
The finest cloth under the world. Our collectors' widows thank you for your custom.
One barrel of milk, several fine stacks of cheese. A dwarf invented it; we merely perfected it.
Never raw. Never brewed. Always delicious. Ask the hospital why.
Know what your mug is worth before the merchant tells you. Artifacts not appraised: we know our limits.
Somebody in a strange mood is asking for something you don't have. We have it. Hurry.
Bone, wood or metal, we polish them all. Artifacts at the owner's risk.
A MARKSDWARF WITHOUT BOLTS IS A DWARF WITH A STICK
Bone or metal, by the hundred. The bowyer never sleeps.
{squads} squads take turns at the barracks. On your month off, rest with us. Beds, mugs and no shouting.
WE SELL NOTHING. YOUR ANIMALS EAT MOSS.
Cave moss spreads on underground soil once the caverns are open. Your herd will be fine. We are going out of business.
Eggs in store this week: {eggs}. Boil them, fry them, or let them hatch and argue with the turkeys.
Why burn charcoal when the world will burn for you? Fire imp repellent sold separately.
Every exposed aquifer tile weeps into its neighbours. Ours weep into buckets.
Know your Granite from your Obsidian. Printed in stone, refreshed every first of Granite.
They grow in any season, underground, on any mud. The fastest way from empty to fed.
Down to {drinks}? We will brew anything that grows, except quarry bushes. Quarry bushes we will cook.
GOBLINS RIDE THEM. WE STOP THEM.
Spikes, walls and a strongly worded sign. Effective against goblins who can read.
It is raining up top. Our coats keep you dry from the gate to the gate.
The only drink in the world not made from a plant. Warm your beard by the hearth.
Elven caravans trade in spring. Hide the wooden furniture. Display the stone.
Humans trade in summer and like bronze, cloth and anything shiny. We have {cloth} cloth. Act now.
Our own caravans come in autumn. They pay in coin, complain in Dwarvish, and drink our stores dry.

classifieds.text: Bones, shells, cloth or gems, for a citizen in a strange mood at the {moody_shop}. Leave at the door. Do not knock.
One {moody_shop}, slightly haunted by genius. Available now that {artifact_maker} has finished with it.
Engraver for a memorial slab. Subject: {lastdead}. Urgent: the fort would rather not meet them again.
One mug, property of the late {lastdead}. Finder may keep it if they fill it once in their memory.
Thread. A great deal of thread. {thread} units of it, to be exact. Make an offer; make any offer.
Kittens. Several. Need no food, climb everything, will adopt you whether you want it or not.
Soap. For the hospital. Also for the east corridor. Also, frankly, for the barracks.
Cave moss inspection for indoor pastures. Spoiler: it is growing. Your herd is fine. Fee: one mug.
A dwarf who knows the difference between a troglodyte and a crundle, to stand at the cavern door and shout the right word.
Lonely goat seeks companionship in a well-mossed pasture. Enjoys grazing, staring and stairs.
Brewing tutorials. One plant makes five drinks. Lesson two: drink them.
Barrels. Empty ones. The still has plants and a brewer and nowhere to put the wine.
Quarry bush leaves, bagged, uncooked. Not to be eaten raw. Not to be brewed. Not to be argued about.
My sense of direction, somewhere on level {depth}. If found, please lead it upstairs.
Training dummy, sturdy, with a forgiving nature. {squads} squads on rotation and the old one has applied for retirement.
Midwifery and babysitting. Infants carried to work at no extra charge. Forges and battlefields declined.
Wedding gifts, mostly rocks, slightly used. Ask for the newlyweds.
Somebody to explain the calendar to the newcomers: twelve months, twenty-eight days each, spring starts on the first of Granite. Patience required.
To the merchants of {caravan_civ}: the depot is open, the broker is awake, and the prices are, as ever, outrageous.
Bees. Any number. For mead, the only drink not made from a plant.
Plump helmets, surplus, by the barrel. We are drowning in them. Please rescue us.
Vampire spotting. We watch who skips meals and sleep. Fee: discreet.
One crossbow bolt, last seen heading for {enemy}. If found, please return it, point first.
Masons, any skill, for the {stone} stones lying in the halls. Turn them into something before somebody trips.
Gems, rough, in quantity: we have {gems}. Cutters wanted; setters preferred.
Smiths, with ore. We have {bars} bars and a militia with opinions.
Miasma removal. Bring us your rotten, your forgotten, your roast left under a bed.
{citizen} wishes to apologise to the carp. The carp has not responded.
Gatherers for the surface, any weather except this one.
Snow shovellers, for the gate. Warm boots supplied. Warm feet not guaranteed.

notices.text: Please do not disturb the {moody_shop}.
{artifact_new} is on display. Look, admire, move along.
Slab for {lastdead} in progress. Masons, take your time; get it right.
Cats need no feeding. Please stop feeding the cats.
The cavern doors stay shut.
Thread orders suspended until further notice.
No quarry bush leaves in the salad.
Brewers: one plant, five drinks. Keep going.
Last barrels: ration with dignity.
Stores are low. Farmers to the plots.
The hospital needs soap.
Bury your dead or meet them again.
Training rota posted at the barracks.
The depot is quiet. The broker naps.
Merchants at the depot. Brokers to your posts.
Rain above. Dry below. As designed.
Snow at the gate. Watch your step.
Welcome, newcomers. Beds are coming.
Quiet in the nursery, please.
Congratulations to the newlyweds.
Haul your refuse. Miasma is everyone's problem.
Masterworks: handle with care.
New Year falls on the first of Granite.
Pig tails: plant before autumn ends.
Sweet pods: spring and summer only.
No caravans in winter. Plan ahead.
Peace holds. Train anyway.
At war with {enemy}. Doors shut.
Grazers on moss: all is well.
Mind the aquifer.

almanac.text: {month}, in the {season}. Plump helmets will grow; so will the list of chores.
Spring: the elven caravans set out, sweet pods go in, and the first of Granite starts the year.
Summer: humans on the roads, pig tails and sweet pods in the plots, and the brook running warm.
Autumn: the dwarven caravan comes from the Mountainhomes, and the last pig tails are planted.
Winter: no caravans on the roads, plump helmets still in the plots, and the river, in colder lands, a floor.
Twenty-eight days to every month, three months to every season, and not one day off.
A dwarf drinks about five times a season. Plan the brewing accordingly.
A caravan leaves twenty-five to thirty-three days after it arrives, with about four days' warning.
Forgotten beasts are drawn by wealth and noise; titans by wealth and numbers. Keep at least one of the four low.
Werebeasts change at the full moon. Check the sky, if you can find it.
Ghosts may rise within three months of an unburied death. The masons have three months.
Miasma only forms underground. Above ground, rot is the sky's problem.
The fort is {fort_days} days old today.
Weather: {weather}. Below ground: dark, damp, delightful.

trivia.text: Did you know? Every artifact in the world was made by a dwarf in a strange mood, and no dwarf makes more than one in a lifetime.
Did you know? A dwarf in a strange mood will not stop to eat, drink or sleep. Only the birth of a child interrupts the work, and then only briefly.
Did you know? Moods come in five kinds: fey, secretive, possessed, fell and macabre. Only the last two are a worry, and they are a big one.
Did you know? Brewing turns every plant into five units of drink, whatever the brewer's skill, and gives the seed back.
Did you know? Cooking a plant destroys its seed. Brewing it, or eating it raw, does not.
Did you know? Plump helmets can be planted in any season, and are the only plant food that can be bought for an embark.
Did you know? Honey brews into mead, the only drink in the world not made from a plant or fruit.
Did you know? Fortress cats and dogs need no food. Cats are born legendary climbers.
Did you know? Modern carp are nearly as heavy as a dwarf and entirely harmless. Their ancestors were not.
Did you know? Giant cave spiders are the size of grizzly bears and live in the deeper caverns.
Did you know? Crundles arrive in packs of fifteen to twenty, and every one is born an adult.
Did you know? Fire imps come up from the magma sea in groups of three or four and throw fireballs.
Did you know? A world like ours has three cavern layers, and they have open edges, so creatures wander in and out.
Did you know? Once a cavern with cave moss is opened, the moss can spread over any underground soil, which is why an indoor pasture works.
Did you know? Elves trade in spring, humans in summer, dwarves in autumn, and nobody trades in winter.
Did you know? A caravan that can't find a path to the trade depot won't come in at all.
Did you know? A fort elects a mayor, usually its most sociable dwarf, once it reaches fifty citizens.
Did you know? The outpost liaison lives at the capital and visits each year to agree what the next caravan brings.
Did you know? Unmet needs cost a dwarf focus, and an unfocused dwarf makes worse crafts and parries worse.
Did you know? A dwarf who is not buried or memorialised may return as a ghost to haunt the place where they died.
Did you know? Prepared meals count as every one of their ingredients when it comes to a dwarf's favourite foods.
Did you know? A dwarf who drinks the same booze too often gets tired of it, and says so.
Did you know? Vampires never eat, drink or sleep, and sometimes arrive hidden in a migrant wave.
Did you know? Titans are the surface cousins of forgotten beasts, and both are made fresh for every world.
Did you know? Magma forges, smelters and glass furnaces need no fuel at all.
Did you know? Sweet pods grow only in spring and summer; pig tails only in summer and autumn.
Did you know? A dwarf who makes an artifact gains a huge leap in skill in that craft, often straight to legendary.
Did you know? Performers entertain at taverns and temples alike, with stories, dance, poetry and music.
Did you know? Libraries need bookshelves for books and chests for writing materials, and a reader leaves with a happy thought.
Did you know? A hospital keeps its own thread, cloth, splints, crutches, plaster, buckets and soap.
Did you know? This fort holds {drinks} drinks, {meals} meals and {plants} plants as of this edition.

proverbs.text: One plant, five mugs, and the seed comes home.
Cook the helmet, lose the spawn.
The cat chooses the dwarf.
Dig deep, dig quiet.
Bury the dead or set a place for them.
A mood waits for nothing, least of all you.
Wealth draws the beast; noise shows it the way.
No caravan comes in winter, and no excuse does either.
The same old booze is a fine reason to brew a new one.
A masterwork lost is a grudge found.
Spring for elves, summer for men, autumn for kin.
Never eat a quarry bush raw twice.
The deeper the stair, the hotter the welcome.
A crundle alone is a joke; twenty is a story.
Moss feeds the goat; the goat feeds the fort.
Thread spun is not cloth woven.
A dwarf without focus parries the air.
Every artifact is one dwarf's whole life, made small.
When the merchants give four days' notice, take three.
The carp forgives; the ankle does not.

ears.text: Brewed with five mugs to the plant

help_wanted.text: BREWER: one plant in, five drinks out. Must enjoy arithmetic and the smell of fermenting mushrooms.
TAVERN KEEPER: pour drinks, break up brawls, remember everyone's name and none of their secrets.
PERFORMER: poets, dancers, storytellers and musicians wanted for the tavern and the temple. Heckling hazard pay available.
SCRIBE: copy books for the library. Must have a steady hand and a tolerance for miners who nap on the shelves.
DOCTOR: diagnosis, surgery, bone setting and sutures. Must not faint. Soap provided, eventually.
WEAVER: {thread} units of thread are waiting. Looms provided. Patience essential.
BUTCHER: the herd is large, the meat stores are small. Steady hands, strong stomach.
FISHERDWARF: the carp are harmless now, the pay is fair, and the river is right there.
MASON: slabs and coffins, urgently. The catacombs must be ready.
GEM CUTTER: {gems} rough gems await. Eyes like a hawk, hands like a surgeon.
CAVERN SCOUT: report on crundles, troglodytes and anything larger. Hazard pay, and a door that locks.
FARMER: plump helmets in any season, pig tails in summer and autumn. Muddy boots supplied.
BROKER: the merchants are here and somebody has to haggle. Must know fine from superior at twenty paces.
SOLDIER: {squads} squads train on rotation through the year. Join one; get every other month to complain about it.

weather_jokes.text: Rain over {fort}. The gatherers are wet, the farms below are as damp as ever, and the cats have gone back to bed.
Heavy weather up top. Down here: the usual drip, the usual dark, the usual complaining.
Snow at the gate. In colder lands the river becomes a floor; in ours it becomes an excuse.
Clear skies over {fort}. Somebody will suggest a picnic. Somebody will suggest it at the cavern door. Do not go.
Fine and clear, {season}. Perfect weather for staying underground and hearing about it.
Forecast for the caverns: dark, damp, with a chance of crundles.
Forecast for level {depth}: warm, and getting warmer.
{season}: no change below ground. There never is. That is the whole point.
In evil lands it rains blood and worse. Here, it merely rains. Count your blessings, and your buckets.
Winter weather reported. No caravans on the roads until spring, so the broker has gone into hibernation.

corrections.text: In yesterday's Bestiary we described the carp as 'harmless'. One reader's ankle has written in to disagree. We stand by the scholars.
We wrongly reported that cats need feeding. They do not. We apologise to the cats, who were insulted, and to the cook, who was relieved.
A notice in our last edition suggested quarry bush leaves 'make a nice salad'. They do not. They must be cooked. The hospital has asked us to say this twice. They must be cooked.
Our obituaries page shortened a cause of death to a single word. We have restored the full wording, which the family preferred.
We said the elven caravan comes in autumn. Elves come in spring; our own kin come in autumn. The broker, who was waiting in the wrong season, has been informed.
We misreported the number of days in a year as 365. It is 336. Our correspondent has been sent back to school, which is also 336 days long.
Our report on the mood at the {moody_shop} described it as 'probably fine'. We have been asked to stop saying 'probably'.
We named the wrong maker for {artifact_new}. It was {artifact_maker}. We regret the error and the shouting.

scores.text: Plump Helmets 5, Brewer 1 (drinks five to one)

sports.head: TRAINING ROTATION ENTERS ANOTHER MONTH
sports.body: With {squads} squads taking turns at the barracks, the fort has a soldier awake at every hour of every day. Our sporting correspondent watched one sparring session and has asked for a cushion.

sports.head: TAVERN BRAWL ENDS IN A DRAW
sports.body: The keeper broke it up, the performers kept playing, and both parties bought the other a drink, which they then threw. Officials have ruled it a draw and the keeper has ruled them both out until next week.

sports.head: CAT CLIMBING CHAMPIONSHIP: EVERYONE WINS
sports.body: Every cat is born a legendary climber, which made the judges' job difficult. All {cats} entrants were awarded first place. The judges were awarded scratches.

sports.head: CRUNDLE HUNT CALLED OFF FOR LACK OF CRUNDLES
sports.body: The militia arrived at the cavern ready for a pack of twenty. They found one, and it ran. Season standings unaffected.
